native_generation_prompt:
Produce a high-detail, professional editorial illustration on pure white, exact wide 1200 by 630 composition. A topographic evidence cutaway with a split registry and prior-paper overlay that meet at a correction boundary. Palette: Indigo and ochre. Hand-colored cartographic engraving with stippled terrain in deliberate coarse marks, muted indigo and ochre, restrained letterforms and no textures resembling writing. White editorial field and advanced textbook object mechanisms with a clear hierarchy. Keep all text glyphs above y565, even for long labels. Source-bound facts: LiDAR analysis flagged a candidate, and the checked registry did not list it. A later literature match showed researchers had already mapped the same site, so the author corrected the claim. Show these meaningful structures: Canopy slice, ground-return slice, terrain profile, plaza geometry, candidate footprint, registry volume, empty registry slot, separate paper folio, earlier map overlay, common footprint boundary, original claim leaf and corrected claim leaf. Draw one arrow from the earlier mapped footprint to the corrected claim leaf. Leave the gap and caveats outside the arrow path. The detached caveat should be well above the 40px bottom floor and entirely isolated from connectors. Type must be strong dark, priority 40px+ and secondary 32px+, maximum visibility, 52px inset. Print each exact label once, only these strings: ["LiDAR candidate","Registry gap","Prior mapping","Rediscovery claim"]. Any other surfaces are completely blank. No exact coordinates, validated archaeological discovery or implication that a registry gap establishes novelty. The registry gap cannot connect directly to a discovery verdict. No logos, human figures, faces, photos, scenery, chart bars, decorative switches, letter-like strokes, panels of generic icons, extra arrows or marks.
